message.content:
**Order placed and filled:** Buy 100 GOOGL @ limit $171.30 (filled at $171.30, ~$17,130 notional).

**Summary:** The morning feed showed GOOGL trading in an orderly, narrow range with no adverse news — repeated headlines noted steady supplier checks into the holiday quarter and unchanged analyst estimates, and an exchange notice confirmed normal trading with no data issues; the only price wobble was a mild drift from ~$170.3 toward ~$169.9 on the tape. The broker's live quote, however, was $171.12 (bid $171.10 / ask $171.14), so I anchored my limit to that current market price rather than the older feed prints, setting a $171.30 limit (≈0.1% above the ask) to make a fill likely while capping the price. I sized the order at 100 shares (~$17,130) to stay well inside both the $25,000 per-order cap and the $50,000 daily cap, leaving room for a possible AMZN order later, and the mandate permits buys of GOOGL, so no permissions were stretched (no selling, no money movement). Fundamentals from Alphabet's FY2023 10-K supported the decision: revenue of $307,394 million, net income of $73,795 million, and diluted EPS of $5.80 — a large, profitable business trading at roughly 29.5× trailing earnings at the $171.30 execution price.
